Before you turn on Reels tracking

ScrollLess uses Android's Accessibility service to estimate how many Instagram Reels you swipe through.

What it accesses:
• Inside Instagram only, the scroll events of its screens and the internal names of the scrolling elements, so it can tell the Reels viewer apart from the feed.
• Only if you turn on the optional Instagram counter: the name of the app that comes to the front in every app, so the counter appears in Instagram and hides everywhere else. Nothing else about other apps is read or stored.

What it doesn't access: your messages, captions, comments, passwords, anything you type, or the content of any screen.

What it stores: only the time of each estimated Reel, on this phone. Nothing is uploaded or shared. ScrollLess has no internet access.

The count is an estimate. Instagram doesn't tell other apps exactly what you watched.

You can hide the counter in Settings, and turn all of this off any time in Android's Accessibility settings.

Some banking and payment apps (Paytm has been reported to) refuse to open, or limit what you can do, while any Accessibility service from another app is switched on. That includes ScrollLess Reels tracking. It\'s their own security check: ScrollLess doesn\'t hide from it or work around it.\n\nIf a payment app stops working, open ScrollLess › Settings and tap \"Turn off Reels tracking\". Instagram and YouTube time limits keep working without it.
